notes: Fresh checks for the South Australia SARIG surface samples (AUSTRALIA_SA_SARIG, phase 1: surface lab assays only) loaded 16 Nov 2026. Not part of the gate.

questions.q: What geochemistry do you have for South Australia?
questions.judge: Describes the SARIG surface samples (AUSTRALIA_SA_SARIG): about 480,000 surface samples with laboratory assays (soil including calcrete, rock, stream sediment, lag, vegetation), about 8 million results, mostly exploration-company data from the 1960s-2020s, and says drill-hole samples are not loaded yet. Credits the Geological Survey of South Australia / SARIG (CC BY 4.0). May mention other sources with SA samples. Does not invent counts.

questions.q: Where are the highest gold values in South Australian calcrete samples?
questions.judge: Uses AUSTRALIA_SA_SARIG samples whose sample_type_local marks calcrete, gives the highest Au values (ppb or ppm, with units) with locations (coordinates or place / region names) and ideally the company or method, from the data. Notes that methods / labs differ (compare like with like) and that calcrete gold values are low-level (ppb) anomaly indicators. Credits SARIG / Geological Survey of South Australia. Does not invent values.

questions.q: Which exploration companies collected the most surface geochemistry samples in South Australia?
questions.judge: Queries AUSTRALIA_SA_SARIG sample comments ('collected by <company>') and lists the top companies with sample counts from the data (counts must be plausible and sum to no more than about 480,000). Credits SARIG / Geological Survey of South Australia. Does not invent companies or counts.
